diagram_math_checks.justification: Lines 44–45 define A=(((U⊗V)⊗W)⊗X), B=((U⊗(V⊗W))⊗X), C=((U⊗V)⊗(W⊗X)), D=U⊗((V⊗W)⊗X), E=U⊗(V⊗(W⊗X)). The five edges are A→C, C→E, A→B, B→D, D→E. Each replaces exactly one ((P⊗Q)⊗R) by P⊗(Q⊗R), as required by the defining convention at line 33.
A→B applies Phi on U,V,W and fixes X, so acts by Phi⊗1. D→E fixes U and applies Phi on V,W,X, so acts by 1⊗Phi. This is precisely the direction of Phi in line 33.
The three blocks are U,(V⊗W),X. The middle Phi component acts on V⊗W by the explicitly stated tensor-product action at line 43, producing (id⊗Delta⊗id)(Phi). Its codomain is D.
The three blocks are (U⊗V),W,X. The first Phi component acts on U⊗V via Delta, giving (Delta⊗id⊗id)(Phi); left-to-right reassociation gives C.
The three blocks are U,V,(W⊗X). The third Phi component acts on W⊗X via Delta, giving (id⊗id⊗Delta)(Phi); left-to-right reassociation gives E.

For left actions, applying p and then q gives qp. Therefore A→B→D→E acts by (1⊗Phi)(id⊗Delta⊗id)(Phi)(Phi⊗1), and A→C→E acts by (id⊗id⊗Delta)(Phi)(Delta⊗id⊗id)(Phi). Their equality is exactly the unchanged pentagon axiom at line 32. The local consumer thm-quasi-bialgebra-modules-form-a-monoidal-category, proof step 2.1, independently spells out these same products; it was read as context only and not changed.
